P0171.description: System Too Lean (Bank 1) – ECM determines from O2 sensor feedback and fuel trim data that the air-fuel mixture is leaner than the stoichiometric 14.7:1 ratio on engine Bank 1.
typical_causes: MAF sensor contamination or aging causing under-reporting of intake air mass
Vacuum leak (intake manifold gasket, cracked vacuum hose, brake booster line)
Weak fuel injector (partially clogged – low flow rate)
Low fuel pressure (failing fuel pump or clogged fuel filter)
O2 sensor bias toward lean due to aging or exhaust leak near sensor
PCV system failure pulling excessive unmetered air
Stuck-open EGR valve admitting unmetered exhaust gas
diagnostic_priority_order: Check LTFT – if >+10% suspect air leak or MAF under-read
Inspect MAF sensor for oil contamination (often from oily air filter)
Smoke test intake for vacuum leaks
Check fuel pressure at rail (spec 45–55 psi at idle for MPFI)
Inspect fuel injectors for pulse width / flow balance
Check O2 sensor switching rate and bias voltage
Inspect EGR valve and position sensor

repair_procedures.action: Inspect air filter and MAF sensor housing for dirt, oil film, or debris
repair_procedures.verification: After cleaning, check live LTFT at idle – should return toward 0% within 2 drive cycles

repair_procedures.action: Smoke test intake manifold and all vacuum lines for leaks
repair_procedures.verification: No smoke visible at any joint; manifold vacuum stable ≥18 inHg

repair_procedures.action: Check fuel pressure at Schrader valve on fuel rail
repair_procedures.verification: Pressure 43–58 psi at idle, drops <2 psi in 10 min key-off soak

repair_procedures.action: Perform injector balance test or flow bench check
repair_procedures.tool: OBD scanner with injector balance test / noid light
repair_procedures.verification: All injectors within 5% flow rate of each other

repair_procedures.action: Replace MAF sensor if cleaning did not resolve LTFT deviation
repair_procedures.tool: Torx T20 screwdriver, wiring harness connector
repair_procedures.verification: LTFT returns to ±5% within two drive cycles after replacement

P0174.description: System Too Lean (Bank 2) – same mechanism as P0171 but for the second bank of a V-engine configuration.
typical_causes: Vacuum leak specific to Bank 2 intake runners or valley cover
Bank 2 MAF sensor or split-design VAF fault
Bank 2 fuel injectors weak or clogged
Single-bank O2 sensor fault biasing LTFT
Common power/ground fault affecting both banks simultaneously (if P0171 also present)
diagnostic_priority_order: Compare Bank 1 and Bank 2 LTFT – if both lean, common-cause fault (MAF, fuel pressure)
If only Bank 2 lean: localized vacuum leak or injector issue
Smoke test Bank 2 intake manifold separately
Check Bank 2 O2 sensor heater resistance (spec 2–30 Ω)
Balance test Bank 2 injectors

repair_procedures.action: Compare Bank 1 vs Bank 2 LTFT live data – if both >+10%, treat as P0171 (common cause)
repair_procedures.verification: Bank 1 LTFT within ±5%, Bank 2 elevated confirms localized fault

repair_procedures.action: Smoke test Bank 2 intake valley and manifold gaskets
repair_procedures.verification: No smoke egress on Bank 2 side

repair_procedures.action: Test Bank 2 O2 sensor heater circuit continuity and response time
repair_procedures.verification: Heater resistance 2–30 Ω; sensor reaches closed-loop within 90 sec of cold start

repair_procedures.action: Flow-test Bank 2 injectors – replace or clean if >5% flow deviation
repair_procedures.tool: Injector flow bench or ultrasonic cleaner
repair_procedures.verification: Flow balance within 3% across all Bank 2 injectors

P0300.description: Random/Multiple Cylinder Misfire Detected – ECM's misfire monitor detected misfires that are distributed randomly across multiple cylinders rather than isolated to one.
typical_causes: Degraded or worn spark plugs (electrodes worn, gap >0.045 in)
Weak ignition coil pack output (all coils share a common module)
Low fuel pressure causing multiple cylinder lean misfire
Vacuum leak causing lean mixture across all cylinders
Retarded ignition timing
EGR stuck open – excessive inert gas dilution
Low compression on multiple cylinders (timing chain stretched)
diagnostic_priority_order: Check for any other co-occurring DTCs (P0171/P0174 suggests lean cause)
Inspect spark plugs – look for fouling, worn electrodes, cracked porcelain
Check ignition coil output voltage (spec ≥40 kV peak)
Verify fuel pressure under load (should not drop below 40 psi at WOT)
Perform compression test (spec typically 150–200 psi, <10% variation)
Check timing chain stretch via cam/crank correlation test

repair_procedures.action: Read all stored DTCs; if P0171/P0174 present, address lean condition first
repair_procedures.verification: Root lean DTC resolved before proceeding to spark/ignition

repair_procedures.action: Remove and inspect all spark plugs; measure gap with feeler gauge
repair_procedures.verification: Gap within OEM spec (typically 0.032–0.044 in); no fouling or erosion

repair_procedures.action: Test ignition coil pack primary/secondary resistance
repair_procedures.verification: Primary 0.5–2.0 Ω, secondary 6–15 kΩ; replace if out of spec

repair_procedures.action: Check fuel pressure at idle and under snap-throttle load
repair_procedures.verification: ≥43 psi idle, does not drop below 40 psi during WOT snap

repair_procedures.action: Compression test all cylinders
repair_procedures.verification: All cylinders ≥150 psi, <10% variation

P0301.description: Cylinder 1 Misfire Detected – ECM detected misfire events exceeding threshold specifically on cylinder 1.
typical_causes: Cylinder 1 spark plug fouled, worn, or cracked
Cylinder 1 coil-on-plug (COP) failure
Cylinder 1 fuel injector clogged or leaking
Low compression in cylinder 1 (worn rings, damaged valves)
Cylinder 1 plug wire failure (if non-COP)
diagnostic_priority_order: Swap Cylinder 1 COP coil to Cylinder 2; if misfire moves to P0302, coil is faulty
Inspect/replace Cylinder 1 spark plug
Check Cylinder 1 injector pulse width and fuel delivery
Compression + leakdown test on Cylinder 1

repair_procedures.action: Swap Cylinder 1 COP to Cylinder 2, clear DTCs, test drive
repair_procedures.verification: Misfire DTC moves to P0302 → coil confirmed faulty; replace Cylinder 1 coil

repair_procedures.action: Remove Cylinder 1 spark plug; inspect for fouling, gap, cracks
repair_procedures.verification: Gap 0.032–0.044 in; no carbon or oil fouling

repair_procedures.action: Check Cylinder 1 injector with noid light and oscilloscope
repair_procedures.verification: Clean square-wave pulse; no short or open

repair_procedures.action: Compression + leakdown test Cylinder 1
repair_procedures.verification: >150 psi compression; <15% leakdown

P0302.description: Cylinder 2 Misfire Detected – ECM detected misfire events exceeding threshold specifically on cylinder 2.
typical_causes: Cylinder 2 COP failure
Fuel injector partial clog (reduced spray pattern)
Cylinder 2 intake valve deposits restricting flow
Spark plug fouled with oil (valve stem seal leak)
diagnostic_priority_order: Swap COP coil from Cylinder 2 to another; misfire follows coil → replace
Inspect Cylinder 2 plug for oil fouling (indicates valve seal issue)
Injector cleaning or replacement
Compression test

repair_procedures.action: COP swap test (same as P0301 Step 1)
repair_procedures.verification: Misfire follows coil → replace

repair_procedures.action: Inspect plug for oil fouling; check valve stem seal
repair_procedures.verification: No oil on plug; blue smoke test negative

repair_procedures.action: Injector balance test / ultrasonic clean
repair_procedures.verification: Flow within 3% of spec

P0303.description: Cylinder 3 Misfire Detected – ECM detected misfire events exceeding threshold specifically on cylinder 3.
typical_causes: Cylinder 3 COP failure (most common)
Cylinder 3 spark plug end-of-life
Fuel injector restricted
Low compression or head gasket breach between cylinders 3 and adjacent
diagnostic_priority_order: COP swap test
Spark plug inspection
Leakdown test with adjacent cylinder comparison
Injector balance test

repair_procedures.action: COP swap test
repair_procedures.verification: Misfire follows coil

repair_procedures.action: Inspect plug and gap
Leakdown test; listen for air in adjacent cylinder
repair_procedures.verification: <15% leakdown; no cross-cylinder pressure

P0304.description: Cylinder 4 Misfire Detected – ECM detected misfire events exceeding threshold specifically on cylinder 4.
typical_causes: Cylinder 4 COP failure
Low compression (common on rear cylinder due to cooling differences)
Head gasket failure (combustion chamber sealed to coolant)
Cylinder 4 injector failure
diagnostic_priority_order: COP swap test
Check for white smoke / coolant loss (head gasket)
Compression + leakdown
Injector check

repair_procedures.action: COP swap test
repair_procedures.verification: Misfire follows coil

repair_procedures.action: Combustion leak test on coolant reservoir
repair_procedures.tool: Block test kit (combustion gas colorimetric test)
repair_procedures.verification: Fluid stays blue (no combustion gases in coolant)

repair_procedures.action: Compression test Cylinder 4 vs adjacent
repair_procedures.verification: Within 10% of adjacent cylinder

repair_procedures.action: Full leakdown test
repair_procedures.verification: <15% leakdown on Cylinder 4

P0562.description: System Voltage Low – ECM detects battery/charging system voltage below the low-voltage threshold (typically <10.5 V) for more than 30 seconds.
typical_causes: Weak or failing battery (internal resistance too high, CCA below spec)
Failing alternator (output <13.5 V at cruise RPM)
High-resistance battery cable connection (corroded terminal, loose clamp)
Bad ground strap between engine block and chassis/battery negative
Parasitic drain depleting battery faster than alternator charges
diagnostic_priority_order: Load test battery (CCA vs spec – e.g., 600 CCA battery should hold >9.6 V during 15 sec 300A load)
Check alternator output voltage at 2000 RPM (spec 13.5–14.5 V)
Inspect all battery cable terminals for corrosion and tightness
Measure voltage drop across battery cables under load (<0.2 V acceptable)
Check for parasitic draw (should be <50 mA after 20-min sleep)

repair_procedures.action: Battery load test – check CCA and voltage hold under load
repair_procedures.verification: Battery holds ≥9.6 V at rated CCA load for 15 seconds; replace if fails

repair_procedures.action: Check alternator output: battery voltage at idle and 2000 RPM
repair_procedures.verification: 13.5–14.7 V at 2000 RPM with all accessories on

repair_procedures.action: Inspect and clean battery terminals; torque to spec
repair_procedures.verification: Voltage drop across positive cable <0.1 V under load

repair_procedures.action: Check engine ground straps continuity and corrosion
repair_procedures.verification: <0.1 V drop between engine block and battery negative under load

repair_procedures.action: Parasitic draw test – check for abnormal current drain
repair_procedures.tool: Clamp ammeter or DMM in series at battery
repair_procedures.verification: <50 mA after 20-minute key-off sleep period

P0563.description: System Voltage High – ECM detects charging system voltage exceeding the high-voltage threshold (typically >16 V) for more than 30 seconds.
typical_causes: Failing alternator voltage regulator (internal or external) – no longer limiting output
Shorted field winding in alternator rotor
Faulty PCM alternator control output (on smart charging systems)
Incorrect alternator installed (wrong output rating)
diagnostic_priority_order: Measure alternator output at battery terminals with DVM at 2000 RPM
Check alternator field control wire voltage from PCM
Inspect for correct alternator part number
Load-test alternator output under full electrical load

repair_procedures.action: Measure voltage at battery terminals at 1500 RPM
repair_procedures.verification: Should be 13.5–14.7 V; if >15.5 V, alternator regulation failed

repair_procedures.action: Check alternator field terminal voltage from PCM
repair_procedures.verification: Confirm PCM is issuing correct duty cycle command; if no PCM output, check PCM alt control fuse

repair_procedures.action: Replace alternator (regulator internal to most modern alternators)
repair_procedures.verification: Voltage 13.5–14.7 V at all RPM with accessory load

U0100.description: Lost Communication With ECM/PCM 'A' – One module on the CAN bus cannot communicate with the ECM/PCM. May be triggered by ECM power loss, ground fault, or CAN bus wiring fault.
typical_causes: CAN bus wiring fault – broken wire, corroded connector, short to ground or +12V
ECM power supply failure (blown fuse, bad relay)
ECM ground connection failure
Terminating resistor failure (CAN bus should measure 60 Ω between CAN-H and CAN-L)
Water/corrosion ingress into ECM connector
Low system voltage causing ECM to reset or drop off bus
diagnostic_priority_order: Check ECM power and ground fuses (typically B+ and Ign supply fuses in IPDM)
Measure CAN bus resistance (CAN-H to CAN-L) – should be 60 Ω (two 120 Ω terminators in parallel)
Check CAN bus voltage levels (CAN-H ~2.5–3.5 V, CAN-L ~1.5–2.5 V)
Inspect ECM connector for corrosion, bent pins, water intrusion
Wiggle test harness near ECM under OBD live monitoring

repair_procedures.action: Check all ECM-related fuses in underhood fuse box
repair_procedures.verification: All ECM fuses intact; voltage present on ECM B+ pin with key-off

repair_procedures.action: Measure CAN bus termination resistance at OBD-II port pins 6 (CAN-H) and 14 (CAN-L)
repair_procedures.tool: Digital multimeter (resistance mode, key off, connectors disconnected)
repair_procedures.verification: 60 Ω (±5 Ω); if open, one terminator missing; if short, wiring fault

repair_procedures.action: Inspect ECM harness connector – check for corrosion, pushed-back pins
repair_procedures.tool: Pick tool, contact cleaner, pin extraction kit
repair_procedures.verification: All pins fully seated; no green corrosion; contact resistance <0.5 Ω

repair_procedures.action: Perform wiggle test on CAN bus wiring with OBD live data active
repair_procedures.tool: OBD-II scanner with live CAN bus monitoring
repair_procedures.verification: No communication drop-outs during flex/wiggle of harness near ECM and firewall grommet

repair_procedures.action: Scope CAN-H and CAN-L waveforms for signal integrity
repair_procedures.tool: Digital oscilloscope, CAN bus breakout box
repair_procedures.verification: Clean trapezoidal waveform, differential swing 2 V, no ringing or flat spots

P0171+P0174_simultaneous.interpretation: Both banks lean simultaneously → common cause (MAF under-read, low fuel pressure, severe vacuum leak) rather than bank-specific fault

P0171+U0100.interpretation: Lean condition + CAN dropout → suspect common ground fault, especially if batt_voltage low

P0562+U0100.interpretation: Low voltage + CAN dropout → severe power supply issue; ECM dropping off bus due to under-voltage

P0300+P0171.interpretation: Random misfire + lean → misfire is CAUSED by lean mixture, not independent ignition fault; fix lean condition first

multi_cylinder_misfires.interpretation: Misfires on 3+ cylinders → fuel pressure, ignition timing, or vacuum leak more likely than individual coil/plug failures
